newsitem.title: UK: Dow strength lifts U.S. London stocks before data. [CORRECTED 11:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Dow strength lifts U.S. London stocks before data. [CORRECTED 11:00 GMT]

text.p: U.S. stocks in London were steady to slightly higher on Thursday, taking strength from another record close overnight on Wall Street but holding back from a major advance by worries about key U.S. economic data.

In New York, the Dow Jones Industrial Average ended 0.49 percent higher at 5,933.97 points, a record close but off its all-time high of 5,966.02 points set in the session. (Corrects from "all-time high of 5,942.17 points set on October 1".)

The U.S. market was driven by continued interest in technology stocks and financials on the back of the strong Treasury market. That momentum carried over to London, where IBM was up $3/8 at $126-1/8. Other hi-techs were steady.
Dealers called the market well-bid but said investors were hanging back to await the 1230 GMT release of jobless claims and, crucially, Friday's release of payrolls data for September.
Wall Street was expected to open trapped in narrow ranges.
"With these figures coming, people are content to sit back. There is still widespread anticipation of a rate hike, it's just a question of when," one dealer said.
Among other stocks in the spotlight, Toys R Us held overnight gains on news it agreed to buy the operator of Infant and Toddler Superstores in a deal valued at $376 million.
